patch.value: GH-1778: pm context extension_health reports ok for packages with a known update and prints same-named project and global copies as identical rows

GH-1778 (filed 2026-11-24). pm context ends with an extension_health block whose rows are {name,status}: status comes only from static discovery, so a package with a known newer registry version reads ok, and a package installed in both project and global scope prints two identical rows with nothing saying which copy the runtime loads (project shadows global by name in buildEffectiveExtensions). pm context is the orientation call agents run first, so ok: 3 reads as nothing to do; the report's hub ran extensions seven weeks behind for that reason. Constraint: pm context must stay offline and fast, and update lookups are network calls that pm package manage and pm package doctor make but never persist (last_update_remote_version is documented as never persisted). Companion finding in the same command: an invalid --section value is refused with a recovery bundle that lists only 8 of the 10 valid sections and says allowed_values_omitted: 2 (complete domain via SDK error.context.recovery.allowed_values), which a CLI agent cannot read; the human Next steps line lists all 10. Small closed domains should print whole. Reproduced on 2026.11.25. Duplicate check: searched extension_health update available shadowed scope, recovery allowed values omitted; no open owner.

extension_health rows carry name, scope, version and status, plus the last observed newer registry version as update when one is known, without any network call from pm context; The summary carries updates_available and a next hint naming the update command only when that count is above zero; A copy shadowed by a same-named copy in another scope is marked shadowed_by instead of repeating an identical row; A refused enumerated value whose whole domain is small prints every allowed value in the recovery bundle, with no omitted counter
pm context tells an agent which installed packages have known updates and which copy is active, offline, and a refused section lists every valid section

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Implementation: pm package manage records what each answered freshness check saw in the untracked runtime/extension-update-observations.json of its scope (failed or timed-out lookups record nothing and keep the earlier observation; a failed write only warns extension_update_observation_write_failed). pm context reads the observations offline: rows {name,scope,version,status,update,shadowed_by}, summary updates_available plus next (one pm package upgrade command per scope) only when the count is above zero; an observation applies only to the installed version it was taken against. Sandbox reproduction of the report (pm-github project 2026.10.4 + global 2026.10.14, observed 2026.11.23): global row shadowed_by project, project row update 2026.11.23, next pm package upgrade pm-github --project. Companion finding: human recovery prints a legal domain of 12 or fewer values whole at the unbudgeted limit, so pm context --section bogus lists all 10 sections; budgeted renderings keep their limits. Cost, from the context-intent calibration report (accepted update): context intent 770 to 793 tokens (2-item fixture) and 1,038 to 1,084 (2,243-item fixture), session orientation 3,495 to 3,518 and 8,182 to 8,205 of 20,000; context stays inside its declared 3,000-token budget.

value.negative_control: tests/unit/commands/query/context-extension-health.spec.ts installs pm-github in project and global scope with an observed newer release and expects shadowed_by, update, updates_available and next; on 2026.11.25 the rows are {name,status} only, both copies read ok with no update and no scope; tests/unit/cli/error-guidance.spec.ts expects the 10 context sections printed whole, where 2026.11.25 prints 8 plus allowed_values_omitted: 2

value.text: Review round 1 (Codex gpt-6.2-sol xhigh: 2 P1, 9 P2, 3 P3; Greptile 4 P2; CodeRabbit 2 minor), all verified against the code and fixed. Observation identity: rows now carry installed_updated_at (the managed record updated_at, which install/upgrade advances whenever the version or source changes), so a commit-only GitHub upgrade retires the observation (Codex P2, Greptile, CodeRabbit). Downgrade guard: a registry latest not newer than the installed version (compareComparableVersions) is recorded as no update. Concurrency: the read-merge-write runs under a per-scope lock (locks/extension-update-observations.lock, 2 s wait, failure only warns) and the later checked_at wins per package (Codex P2, Greptile). File safety: only a bounded (1 MiB) regular file in a real runtime/ directory is read; a link, FIFO or non-directory runtime reads as no knowledge and is never written through (Codex P2). Context: updates_available and next count only the copy the runtime loads (effective layer+directory), so a disabled copy keeps its row but earns no hint (Codex P2, Greptile); hints are rendered from argv with renderPmCommand, keep the selected tracker via resolvePmCommandScopeArgs, and put a dash-leading name after -- (Codex P1 + P2). updates_available is optional on StaticExtensionInventoryResult (always emitted) so SDK fixtures keep type-checking (Codex P3).

value.text: Review round 2 (Codex gpt-6.2-sol xhigh: 1 P1, 10 P2, 5 P3), each verified and fixed. Hints: one targeted command per loaded package (at most five) rendered as pm [--pm-path <absolute tracker>] package upgrade --<scope> --packages-only -- <name>: the name after -- cannot be re-read by the bootstrap key=value normalizer (P1, probed: status=open stays a literal target), --packages-only keeps a lost target from upgrading the CLI, no scope-wide upgrade of unreported packages, the absolute tracker survives SDK cwd swaps, and --no-extensions is never inherited (it would fail activation verification). Writer: under the lock the record is rebuilt from the managed state on disk, keeping the latest observation per current installation and dropping replaced or removed ones, which closes the stale-process overwrite race, bounds the file, and is refused above 1 MiB. Reader: O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK open with fstat and a bounded read on the descriptor (no FIFO hang, no swapped-file widening); runtime/ rechecked after the lock is held; checked_at must parse. Downgrade guard uses SemVer precedence against the installed npm version (prereleases sort first). Context treats corrupt managed metadata as unknown updates instead of failing. Inventory binds identity to the directory's own managed record.

value.text: Review round 3 (Codex: 1 P1, 9 P2, 2 P3). Design change that closes a whole class: next no longer names packages. Each hint is the live, scoped check pm [--pm-path <absolute tracker>] package manage --<scope>, whose remediation names the upgrade, so no manifest-controlled name can select a second installation (manifest name equal to another package's npm name), parse as an option (-- --global, -- --version), or lose its quoting; Markdown renders hints as code spans so CommonMark never consumes shell escapes. Also fixed: local npm artifacts (path or file: specs, shared isLocalNpmSpec rule with upgrade) never get a registry update; the reader lstat-checks the entry before the no-follow open, which covers Windows where O_NOFOLLOW is undefined; the observation lock passes maxWaitMs so PM_LOCK_WAIT_MS cannot stretch the derived write; inventory binds observations to the exact directory. Not changed, with reason: replacing runtime/ with a link between the post-lock recheck and the rename needs write access to the tracker's own runtime directory, which already controls tracker state; Node has no openat for directory-relative I/O, and the recheck plus link refusal bound the window.

value.text: Review round 4 (Codex: 1 P1, 5 P2, 4 P3; Greptile 1; CodeRabbit 3). Fixed: one SemVer verdict for manage and the offline readers (checkNpmUpdate now uses isNewerRegistryVersion, so an older registry latest is no update anywhere, and the collector records the provider verdict as is); npm sources are classified with npm-package-arg plus archive-path rules (bare tarballs, artifacts/pkg.tgz, name@file:, git and URL specs are never registry sources), shared with upgrade source selection; check times more than five minutes ahead read as clock errors; Markdown puts multi-line hints in a fenced block; docs and types describe updates_available and shadowed_by as static selection, not activation truth. Not changed, with reason (second report): runtime/ replaced between the post-lock recheck and the write needs a process that can already rewrite the tracker's own runtime state; Node has no directory-relative file API, and the lifecycle doc now states that residual window instead of promising full confinement.

value.text: Review round 5 (Codex: 1 P1, 3 P2, 3 P3; CodeRabbit 2). Fixed: the observation merge keeps every new answer when managed state is unreadable mid-write (a concurrent lifecycle write), latest per installation, and prunes on the next complete snapshot, instead of discarding the run's answers; rows with a wrong-typed remote_version and records with another envelope version read as no knowledge; checkNpmUpdate and the GitHub check stamp checked_at at completion (the documented contract), so the newest-wins merge orders overlapping checks by when they finished. Follow-up filed: pm-4qq9jy owns recording whether an npm install resolved to a local directory (npm:plugin with a local plugin directory), which needs new managed-source provenance and also affects live manage and upgrade. Not changed, with reason (third report): redirecting runtime/ after the post-lock recheck needs a process that can already rewrite this tracker's runtime state; the write is a fixed-name, pm-generated JSON file; Node has no directory-relative file API; the lifecycle doc states the residual window. Atomic managed-state publication was tried and reverted: it changes the install rollback contract that tests pin, which is outside this PR.

value.text: Review round 6 (Codex: 1 P1, 3 P2, 2 P3), all fixed. Live manage skips the registry lookup for a non-registry npm source and reports it skipped_non_github with reason managed_npm_source_not_registry, so manage and the offline readers agree; npm's own registry verdict now takes precedence over the archive-suffix rule (@scope/plugin.tgz stays a registry package, so upgrade --tag selection keeps working); the observation writer and pm context use a strict managed snapshot (readStrictManagedRecords: every entry must be valid, as the static inventory requires), so a malformed entry never prunes its observation or reports updates from a file the inventory marks invalid; hints for a tracker path ending in whitespace add a trailing /. so the trimmed --pm-path still names it (hint builder moved to sdk/extension/upgrade-hints.ts).

value.text: Review round 7 (Codex: 0 P1, 6 P2, 3 P3). Fixed: readStrictManagedRecords parses, normalizes and counts the same bytes (one read), with only a missing file as an empty snapshot; observation fields longer than 256 characters (far above any name, version, commit or ISO time pm writes) read as no knowledge, so one corrupt row cannot fill the record and block merges; a failed write keeps its typed reason in the warning (extension_update_observation_write_failed:<code>, e.g. a stale lock left by a crashed process) so lock recovery guidance applies; the Markdown summary escapes manifest-controlled degraded names and renders every hint in its own fenced block, so no name can open a code span around a command; the lifecycle doc states that manage and the offline readers never compare git/URL npm sources with the registry and that upgrade reinstalls path, tarball and file: artifacts as they are.

value.text: Review round 8 (Codex: 0 P1, 3 P2, 4 P3). Fixed: the collector records only sources a check actually queries (GitHub, or a registry npm source), so a stale verdict on a skipped record never becomes an observation; shadowed_by uses directory identity, so a losing same-named copy in the same scope is marked; the lifecycle doc now says an install that changes the version or source retires an observation while an identical reinstall keeps it (its answer still applies). Deferred with reason: install-time npm resolution (a bare npm:<name> resolved to a local directory) and the registry a check used (project .npmrc versus the caller's cwd) are both provenance the managed record does not hold; both belong to pm-4qq9jy. A relative PM_GLOBAL_PATH makes a copied --global hint depend on the caller's directory, like every other command run under that override; documented as an environment assumption rather than encoded in the hint.

value.text: Review round 10 (Codex: 0 P1, 2 P2, 3 P3; CodeRabbit 2). Fixed: the observation merge publishes inside lease.fence (acquireLockLease), so a writer whose expired lease was reclaimed refuses with lock_lost instead of overwriting its successor's newer answers; the collector applies the reader's 256-character field bound, so a package with an unusually long manifest version reads as unknown consistently instead of being written and then dropped; the runtime/ swap test waits on an explicit barrier (the first runtime/ check returning) instead of a delay. Re-reported and owned by pm-4qq9jy: install-resolution and registry provenance (CodeRabbit raised the registry half as well).

value.text: Review round 11 (Codex: 0 P1, 4 P2, 2 P3). Fixed: the managed-state reread during an observation merge goes through the guarded bounded reader (entry lstat, no-follow non-blocking descriptor, 16 MiB bound), so a FIFO or endless stream never holds the observation lease; the lifecycle doc no longer says manage names the upgrade: it shows update evidence and its remediation says to reinstall, with pm package upgrade <name> --<scope> as the single-package command. Re-reported, owned elsewhere: SDK/MCP static listing (pm-q5iao5), npm install provenance (pm-4qq9jy).

value.text: Review round 12 (Codex: 0 P1, 5 P2, 1 P3). Fixed: the package lifecycle resolves an MCP/SDK caller's declared scope (scope: global|project|local) like the CLI switches, so package-manage for the global scope records its observations in the global cache (resolveScope previously read only the boolean switches); an expired observation lease from an interrupted check may be reclaimed without force (as session state does), the commit fence still refusing a resumed stale holder; offline readers re-validate a cached verdict against the current managed source (only GitHub and registry npm sources are checked, and an npm update must be SemVer-newer than the installed version), so an edited row cannot mark a local artifact updatable or an older release newer; the static inventory matches observations against the same strict guarded managed snapshot as pm context, so both readers agree. Re-reported, owned elsewhere: SDK list helpers (pm-q5iao5) and npm install provenance (pm-4qq9jy).

value.text: Review round 13 (Codex: 0 P1, 3 P2, 3 P3). Fixed: a cached registry version must be exact SemVer, as checkNpmUpdate requires, before it can count as an update; flat MCP scope hoists on the package and extension actions, so a top-level scope: global selects the global cache like options.scope; the strict MCP schema version bumps to 4.28.1 for the additive fields parameter. Accepted residual, not changed: inventory derives its managed receipts and its observation matching from two reads of .managed-extensions.json, so a lifecycle write landing between them can pair an invalid receipt with an update from the completed file; both reads are individually consistent and the next read agrees, and unifying them would change how inventory treats a symlinked managed-state file.

value.text: Review round 14 (Codex: 0 P1, 4 P2). Fixed: context hints carry a caller's explicit --no-extensions, since the live check in manage runs before its activation probe; the cache reader validates npm versions with the live check's own exact-version rule (npm-package-arg resolves a version spec; isExactNpmVersion), so build metadata such as 2.0.0+build.1 is accepted exactly where the writer can produce it; a GitHub row must carry the hexadecimal commit a repository check records; untrusted labels in the Markdown summary are folded to one line, so an edited cache cannot inject Markdown blocks.

Fixed: the static inventory reads managed state once, bounded and non-blocking and following links like the runtime loader, and that one snapshot serves both the completeness receipt and observation matching (pm context's strict reader follows links the same way); a lock path that is not a regular file refuses the derived observation write instead of hanging on the core lock reader (the cleanup-gate metadata path stays a recorded residual, owned by the core lock); merge candidates the current source could not have produced never win the newest-first pick; loose exact versions npm admits (01.0.0) compare by SemVer precedence; every context hint names the selected tracker (--pm-path), because manage's activation probe resolves it even for a global check; EXTENSION_LIFECYCLE.md documents the fenced-block rendering and the carried --no-extensions; the pm-gh1777 migrate note says installed rows carry update and absent rows omit it. value.text: Review round 16 (Codex: 0 P1, 5 P2, 1 P3), each verified. Fixed: the static enablement and presentation settings reads are bounded, non-blocking and follow a link to a regular file, like the general settings reader, so a FIFO settings.json reads as settings_unreadable instead of hanging and a linked settings file keeps its output and migration-hint defaults; pm package upgrade moves only a registry npm install to the requested tag and reinstalls every path, tarball, file:, git or URL artifact from its own spec, the same policy the freshness check applies; a freshness check under a pinned reproducible clock (PM_CLOCK/PM_SEED) records no observation, because pinned check times cannot order a wall-clock cache nor tell apart two installs that share a pinned updated_at (this also closes the pinned-clock same-commit binding report); the offline reader picks the newest source-consistent row for an installation, as the writer's merge does.

Fixed: the observation write also refuses up front when the core lock's stale-cleanup gate owner file is not a regular file, so malformed lock state is a cache-write warning instead of a hang; the bootstrap command-path scan skips host options before the noun with the shared host-option grammar, so pm --no-changed-fields package list --fields bogus --fields name merges both occurrences and refuses bogus; SDK.md and the runRegisteredCommandForTest docstring say host-owned keys skip extension-option normalization only after host validation, which can still refuse a read-output control. Fixed: the observation spec's file-link case is its own test that skips on win32, and its two directory links use a junction on Windows, which needs no privilege; the size-limit case now uses a valid versioned envelope with a below-limit control that returns the observation, so only the size can reject it. Fixed: the observation write's lock preflight also refuses an oversized lock file or stale-cleanup gate owner file (over 64 KiB), since the core lease reads them whole; the context Markdown replaces every control character (Unicode Cc) in a manifest-controlled label with U+FFFD after folding line breaks, so a shadowed package's version cannot drive the terminal, while the structured values stay exact. value.text: Review round 19 (Codex: 0 P1, 3 P2, 3 P3), each verified. Fixed: a cached registry verdict, positive or negative, must be the one the live check's comparison gives for an exact version it accepts, so an edited negative row can no longer hide a valid update; SDK.md and the runRegisteredCommandForTest docstring say host validation refuses a read-output control on a command that neither declares read_output nor extends a native read contract. Accepted residual: a stalled concurrent holder of the core stale-cleanup gate can delay the derived observation fence and release by the core lock's own waits (about ten seconds each), after the provider checks completed; the write still never publishes without ownership and a failure stays a warning. Repeats with owners: pm-4qq9jy (resolved npm provenance) and pm-q5iao5 (SDK and MCP static listing).
